title: Delegation pre-flight one-shot dispatch
desc: Pre-satisfy ALL delegation guards in one pass so a single dispatch succeeds, instead of discovering the stall/usage/brief/sync/update-gate cascade one block at a time (wasted cache tokens). Opus session lesson 2026-06-03.
steps: WHY THIS EXISTS: a delegation call (Agent / Agent.cmd / wkcodex) passes guards SEQUENTIALLY, each one Block-and-exit on first failure pointing to a different skill. Discovering them one at a time = N round-trips, and every retry re-sends the full conversation context = wasted cache tokens. LIVE proof (Opus 2026-06-03): one delegation hit stall-guard then usage-test-guard then brief-guard then claude-md-sync-guard then update-gate = 5 separate blocks. CURE until the collect-all gate lands: pre-satisfy EVERY precondition BEFORE the first dispatch.

PRE-FLIGHT CHECKLIST (do ALL before dispatching, in this order): one, record the work in CLAUDE.md Pending so claude-md-sync-guard is clear. two, commit any uncommitted tools wkharness source edits so update-gate is clear. three, put 3 or more distinct wkappbot skill read lines in the prompt so agent-brief-guard is clear. four, prefer Agent.cmd over the native Agent tool because a 50 percent usage-test trainer redirects native Agent to Agent.cmd anyway.

TIER EVIDENCE (the dialectic and haiku-trainer evidence gates, stateless from session JSONL): a Sonnet target needs at least 2 Haiku delegations completed in the prior 10 minutes. an Opus target needs at least 2 Haiku plus 1 Sonnet in the prior 10 minutes PLUS a 5 point SPEC block in the prompt. a Haiku or codex-mini target is exempt (it is the floor scout). So spawn the cheap groundwork FIRST, then escalate.

BRIEF-FILE PATTERN (dodges arg-mangling and content-match false-positives): write the full brief to a pace-exempt memory markdown file, then dispatch with a SHORT prompt that says read that memory file and execute it, plus the 3 skill read lines inline. This avoids Agent.cmd heredoc breakage on dashes and non-ASCII, and avoids harness skill path false-fires from literal source paths in a long brief.

OPUS BACKGROUND RULE: when the running session is Opus, every delegation must be launched run-in-background true (foreground delegation is blocked so the user prompt stays responsive). You are notified on completion. Do NOT poll the output file in a loop; that burns tokens and the harness re-invokes you when the task finishes.

PACE DISCIPLINE: bare wk-prefixed commands are pace-exempt. an absolute path or a non-wk command gets pace-blocked when over target. so call WillKim tools by their bare name (for example wkagent-name, not the drive-letter tools path) and route real work through wk wrappers or a delegation.

FUTURE: the collect-all delegation gate (canonical design memory collect-all-spec.md) will batch every unmet precondition into ONE message and a single exit, making this manual checklist automatic. Until it lands, follow this checklist. Cluster siblings: claude-code-agent-tier-routing and opus-self-reflection.

FAILURE-RECOVERY ANCHOR (user directive 2026-06-03): this skill is THE recovery target that every delegation-guard block points to. Goal = when a delegation is blocked, the AI reads ONE checklist and satisfies every precondition in a single retry, instead of discovering guards one at a time. Implementation requirement for the collect-all delegation gate: the single Emit-WkDlgViols message MUST end with a line pointing here (wkappbot skill read delegation-preflight-oneshot), and until collect-all lands each interim delegation block (stall, usage-test, brief, sync, update-gate, haiku-trainer, dialectic, spec-gate, opus-budget) should append the same pointer. Reading this skill on any delegation failure = the one-shot fix.

SONNET/HAIKU LESSON 1 - wkappbot file write = pace-exempt file creator: when Write tool is blocked by pace guard, use 'wkappbot file write <path> --content "..."' instead. It bypasses the pace gate entirely. wkappbot file* commands are always safe. Use for NEW files too, not just edits.

SONNET/HAIKU LESSON 2 - ./wk*.sh is pace-exempt, bash/python is NOT: Bash(python ...) and Bash(bash script.sh) are blocked by wk-only-gate. But Bash(./wkbuild-skills.sh) passes because the leading token starts with wk and is treated as a wk-tool call. Pattern: create a wk-prefixed wrapper script in repo root, then call it as ./wkXXX.sh. This is the escape hatch for any script that wk-only-gate blocks.

SONNET/HAIKU LESSON 3 - exit 0 does NOT mean the task succeeded: wkcodex and Agent.cmd return exit 0 even when they didn't create files or apply edits. ALWAYS verify with Grep/Glob/Read after any delegation that should modify files. Trust but verify every time -- agent summaries describe intent, not actual work.

SONNET/HAIKU LESSON 4 - wkcodex sandbox cannot write outside CWD: wkcodex runs in a workspace-write sandbox and CANNOT create/modify files at absolute paths like D:/GitHub/wkappbot-sdk/docs/. Use Agent.cmd haiku instead for tasks that write to the real filesystem. wkcodex is good for reading code and analysis, not for file creation at fixed paths.

SONNET/HAIKU LESSON 5 - same Edit/fix repeatedly = STOP, switch approach: if the same edit fails 2+ times (pace guard, agent didn't apply, file not found), do NOT retry the same path. Decision tree: (1) pace blocked -> use wkappbot file write or wkappbot file edit. (2) agent didn't write file -> switch from wkcodex to Agent.cmd haiku. (3) Agent.cmd haiku didn't write -> use wkappbot file write directly. Each retry re-sends full context = expensive. Max 2 attempts per approach then pivot.
